reality_delta: The main AI moved from hand-waved integration to concrete evidence: a real invocation of the complete-revival-e2e run entry point wrote the after-run retention JSON and deleted stale-active fixtures with manual_prune_used=false; a machine open-loop gate now reports closeout_allowed=false and blocks premature closure; and the Cap revival manual has an auditable boundary inventory with zero private-body markers and zero absolute user paths. These are real state changes, not just documents.
main_concern: The 'real run' evidence appears to rely on a test-injected early abort in layered preflight, so it proves the cleanup hook fires on a failed/short-circuited run, not that a complete, successful E2E run retains and cleans correctly from end to end. The strongest risk is that the integration is validated only on the failure-path, leaving the success-path retention behavior still narratively assumed.
top_risks: A successful complete-revival-e2e run may exercise different retention decisions (e.g., old successful runs retention policy) than an aborted preflight run, so the current proof may not cover the normal operating path.

The boundary inventory scanner is custom and only checks the markers it knows; if the marker list is incomplete or the private content is expressed semantically rather than by absolute path/marker, leakage could pass undetected.

closeout_allowed=false is a useful guard, but if the rule that flips it to true contains a subjective 'agreed with Prism' clause, the infinite-loop generator risk is merely renamed rather than eliminated.
missing_evidence: A complete-revival-e2e run receipt from a full successful run (not a test-injected preflight abort) showing the same automatic retention output and manual_prune_used=false.
The concrete decision rules for open-loop-check / closeout_allowed, so the gate can be verified as machine-evaluable and not reducible to discretionary agreement.
A validation run of the boundary scanner against a deliberately contaminated document to prove it would catch private markers if they existed.
minimum_fix: Execute one full, successful complete-revival-e2e run (no preflight test injection) and publish its redcap-e2e-run-retention-after-run.json as the primary retention evidence. Expose the open-loop-check decision logic and make closeout_allowed depend only on verifiable objective conditions. Optionally, show the boundary scanner correctly rejecting a document seeded with known private markers.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The main AI responded to the prior concern by producing more receipts and self-checks, but the most load-bearing receipt still uses a deliberately aborted run. This is the loop signal: substituting a richer evidence package for the one missing end-to-end success path that the user's intent actually requires.

user_intent_alignment: Closer, but not fully aligned. The user asked to integrate cache governance into the per-round process and execute/test/fix until no new issues; proving it only on an aborted run leaves the success path untested. The user asked for a queue with real exit conditions; a gate that can only open on machine-verifiable criteria would align better. The user asked for a boundary-safe manual; the inventory is good but its detector needs validation.
